claims.value: The canonical design, created and updated 2026-07-11, is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620 released 2026-06-17, plus SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. Its 54:00 interval from local fire-wave impact to the next impact is a versioned community/game-data model, not an official invariant: Creepy Jar has published no numerical phase formula, although the current starrupture.tools client and an independent runtime-reading open-source mod strongly corroborate it. Manual cycle 0:00 is when the fire wall reaches the player; the moving wave may make the global-to-local offset location-dependent. Allowed confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required. Confidence must be downgraded after a large correction, device-clock change, model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop; no numerical accuracy estimate may appear until measured. The approximately two minutes of white warning, 15 seconds of yellow warning, and final roughly 15-second countdown still require live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation. Until validation, use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—never exact, safe, or guaranteed. The repository foundation is bootstrapped, but historical session 019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334 ended without a final handoff or evidence that simulator/install-ready acceptance passed.

claims.value: The player-facing 54-minute timeline has five states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (Remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (Remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (Lower ambient threat; use the window), World active 11:30-51:30 (ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00 (return, bank loot, and shelter). The reference site folds warning into its 42:30 Stable block, while runtime tooling exposes Warning separately. During recovery the hero countdown targets when ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during normal ecology it targets the next Ruptura or warning start. Portrait must show, without scrolling: (1) sync/capability status, including degraded or unsynced state; (2) semantic hero state, huge monospaced countdown, and explicit target; (3) threat label plus one action sentence; (4) at most two provenance-visible opportunity cards; and (5) exact-time next events with only Mute one cycle and Re-sync always visible. Retain a proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but add equal/minimum-width labeled steps or an event list so the 30-second Burning and 60-second Cooling phases cannot collapse to a few pixels. Landscape/charging places countdown left and threat/opportunity right with no setup controls. Historical interaction evidence records the player selecting direction 3, Mission Timeline, at 2026-07-11 22:54 UTC; that selection is a design decision, not evidence of implementation completion.

claims.value: Enemy-return events and gathering opportunities are separately versioned facts, not universal consequences of phase boundaries. Each OpportunityWindow stores id, start event or offset, end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot; visible provenance is confirmed, community-derived, player-observed, or experimental. Initial cards are: Reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery—Lower ambient threat; triggered encounters may persist; Oxallop in early recovery while lakebeds are dry—gather before water returns; Cave access, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery—favorable, but check rather than guarantee respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery—fresh post-wave gatherable with variable spawn rate; Star Tears in late Recovery with experimental timing—leave some cooled Ignitium unharvested when Star Tears are the priority; Coralion/Vulpir eggs in post-wave Recovery—variable spawn; surface foliage and water during Regrowth/active world—say Regrowth underway, not an exact species timer; and Sulheart only in a fully regenerated world—hide it until exact current timing is validated. The Ignitium/Star Tears tradeoff must be shown as a choice rather than simultaneous certainty. MVP personalization pins two priorities; the current player model favors Oxallop and Prickler over already-overstocked Hydrobulb and Prism Herb, while Glowcaps remain a strategic medicine reserve.

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptic signatures and must never rely on color or audio alone. Default enemy-return ladder: 5 minutes—amber edge, Finish or leave hard POIs, short double haptic/optional tone, normal notification; 2 minutes—persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional normal notification; 1 minute—red instruction with emphasized seconds and stronger distinct cue, background notification off by default to prevent duplication; 15 seconds—static danger border, large seconds, one final cue with no ticking and no background alert; event—ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, and a local notification or explicitly armed alarm. Pre-Ruptura points are optional 10-minute planning, 5-minute finish-the-trip, 2:30 warning start, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. A player-selected exit buffer overrides fixed planning thresholds—for example, seven minutes produces TURN BACK NOW seven minutes before expected enemy return. Provide Full, Haptic only, and Visual only profiles; separate phase, enemy, Ruptura, and opportunity toggles; Mute one cycle; pre-session sound/haptic preview; and collapse missed cues after resume to the strongest current message rather than replaying a backlog. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it afterward; offer dim OLED mode, recommend charging, and never use background audio as keep-alive. Schedule local notifications at absolute dates and reschedule after anchor, model, or policy changes; recompute (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration on every resume; deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. A Live Activity represents only the currently armed event and must not promise indefinite self-advancement without background authority. On iOS 26, AlarmKit may be used only after an explicit Arm loud enemy-return alarm or Watch Session action; it requires authorization and a usage description and must never silently create an endless 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS uses normal local notifications; Time Sensitive is separately opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Text, symbol, border shape, and optional pattern accompany color; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion; prohibit full-screen flashing, default per-second ticking, and per-second VoiceOver announcements; keep Re-sync, Mute one cycle, capability state, and the exact next-alert time visible.
